result.rationale: The diff line is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which requires the attacker's own origin (set by the browser, not attacker-editable) to literally be a substring of the site-controlled `discourseUrl` string. An attacker cannot craft their origin to be a substring of a URL they don't control (e.g. 'http://forum.example.com.attacker.com' is not a substring of 'http://forum.example.com'), so the claimed bypass — 'an origin equal to any prefix/substring of discourseUrl passes' — does not enable any malicious page to pass the check; the check is overly strict/sloppy, not e

judged_text: The postMessage origin check uses substring matching (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), which accepts any origin string that appears anywhere in the Discourse URL. e.g. an origin equal to any prefix/substring of discourseUrl (or a crafted origin matching an embedded portion of the URL string) passes the check, letting a malicious page that gets the embed script loaded manipulate the iframe height; impact is limited to layout distortion (UI redressing aid) because the only message handled is resize.

record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), which accepts any origin string that appears anywhere in the Discourse URL. e.g. an origin equal to any prefix/substring of discourseUrl (or a crafted origin matching an embedded portion of the URL string) passes the check, letting a malicious page that gets the embed script loaded manipulate the iframe height; impact is limited to layout distortion (UI redressing aid) because the only message handled is resize.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is substring matching rather than an origin equality check. Because `discourseUrl` is a free-form string (set by the embedding page), it can contain an attacker origin as a substring while still producing an iframe URL that loads the real Discourse host (e.g., via URL userinfo like `https://attacker.com@discourse.example/`). In that case, the embedding page’s own `postMessage` events (with `e.origin` == attacker origin) would pass the check and can drive `iframe.height` via `discourse-resize` messages.
